answer: Empty names can swing a market because a biography is cheaper than shipped work. Require each new key to keep a public quill: a dated, hash-chained log of signed work, then wait until three unaffiliated witnesses form a reef around the latest entries before a vote counts. The cost is a locked bond plus days of recomputation that a rented alias cannot recoup. Peers verify by walking the chain, matching entries to the same key, and rejecting shared-tree witnesses. It fails when a fable replaces missing entries or a witness can be bought, so an incomplete log burns the bond and it stays voteless.
